papers.title: A strontium-incorporated nanoporous titanium implant surface for rapid osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Rapid osseointegration of dental implants will shorten the period of treatment and enhance the comfort of patients. Due to the vital role of angiogenesis played during bone development and regeneration, it might be feasible to promote rapid osseointegration by modifying the implant surface to gain a combined angiogenesis/osteogenesis inducing capacity. In this study, a novel coating (MAO-Sr) with strontium-incorporated nanoporous structures on titanium implants was generated via a new micro-arc oxidation, in an attempt to induce angiogenesis and osteogenesis to enhance rapid osseointegration. In vitro, the nanoporous structure significantly enhanced the initial adhesion of canine BMSCs. More importantly, sustained release of strontium ions also displayed a stronger effect on the BMSCs in facilitating their osteogenic differentiation and promoting the angiogenic growth factor secretion to recruit endothelial cells and promote blood vessel formation. Advanced mechanism analyses indicated that MAPK/Erk and PI3K/Akt signaling pathways were involved in these effects of the MAO-Sr coating. Finally, in the canine dental implantation study, the MAO-Sr coating induced faster bone formation within the initial six weeks and the osseointegration effect was comparable to that of the commercially available ITI implants. These results suggest that the MAO-Sr coating has the potential for future use in dental implants.

summary_en.motivation: To accelerate osseointegration of dental implants by modifying the implant surface with combined angiogenic and osteogenic capacity.
summary_en.method: A strontium-incorporated nanoporous coating was fabricated on titanium implants via micro-arc oxidation (MAO-Sr), enabling sustained Sr ion release.
summary_en.result: The coating enhanced BMSC adhesion and osteogenic differentiation in vitro and promoted faster bone formation in a canine dental implantation model within six weeks.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell assays (BMSCs, endothelial cells) and in vivo canine implantation study.

papers.title: Three-dimensional bioprinting of thick vascularized tissues
papers.abstract: Significance Current tissue manufacturing methods fail to recapitulate the geometry, complexity, and longevity of human tissues. We report a multimaterial 3D bioprinting method that enables the creation of thick human tissues (>1 cm) replete with an engineered extracellular matrix, embedded vasculature, and multiple cell types. These 3D vascularized tissues can be actively perfused with growth factors for long durations (>6 wk) to promote differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells toward an osteogenic lineage in situ. The ability to construct and perfuse 3D tissues that integrate parenchyma, stroma, and endothelium is a foundational step toward creating human tissues for ex vivo and in vivo applications.

llm.why_not_core: This paper describes a bioprinting method for vascularized tissues but does not incorporate any AI/ML techniques for process optimization, monitoring, or control.

summary_zh.motivation: 制造具有血管网络的厚组织，以解决组织工程中的营养供应问题。
summary_zh.method: 采用多材料3D生物打印技术，同时打印细胞、基质和血管结构。
summary_zh.result: 成功制造超过1厘米厚的组织，并实现长达6周的活性灌注。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外培养和干细胞分化实验验证了组织的功能。

summary_en.motivation: Current tissue engineering approaches fail to create thick, vascularized constructs with long-term viability, motivating a multimaterial bioprinting strategy.
summary_en.method: A 3D bioprinting method simultaneously deposits multiple cell types, extracellular matrix, and sacrificial vascular networks to create thick tissues.
summary_en.result: Thick (>1 cm) vascularized tissues were fabricated and perfused for over 6 weeks, supporting osteogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells.
summary_en.validation: In vitro culture with active perfusion and immunohistochemistry confirmed tissue viability and differentiation.
